sacrificeEvidence.title: Retainer killings in the Royal Cemetery at Ur
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: Human remains in elite funerary contexts support deliberate retainer killing. Changing reconstructions of the deaths remain visible, and Atlas does not describe the dead as willing.
sacrificeEvidence.evidence: Excavation context, skeletal remains, and later reassessment.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Early excavation interpretations and later scholarship used different evidence and methods.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: The mechanism, staging, royal identification, and interpretation have been revised; intent or consent is not inferred.
sacrificeEvidence.confidence: Ritual killing supported; circumstances partly disputed

sacrificeEvidence.title: Livy's report of the Forum Boarium burials in 216 BCE
sacrificeEvidence.period: 216 BCE event reported in a later Roman history
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: Livy reports the live burial of two couples after Cannae. Atlas records the literary report and its chronology without claiming archaeological confirmation.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Livy wrote long after the reported event and shaped it within Roman historiography.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: Historical interpretation and terminology require comparison with other evidence.
sacrificeEvidence.confidence: Text securely attested; event evidence is literary

sacrificeEvidence.title: Carthage tophet interpretation debate
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: Cremated infant remains and inscriptions are documented, while cemetery-versus-sacrifice interpretation and frequency remain disputed.
sacrificeEvidence.evidence: Archaeology, osteology, inscriptions, and ancient literary testimony.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Ancient hostile accounts and preservation/age-estimation limits require separate treatment.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: Published scholars reach different conclusions about sacrifice and mortality profiles.

sacrificeEvidence.title: Caesar's allegation about Druid sacrifice
sacrificeEvidence.period: First century BCE Roman conquest narrative
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: Caesar alleges sacrificial killings in Gallic War 6.16. Atlas presents this as a conqueror's report, not verified generic Druid history.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Caesar was a military conqueror writing about peoples he fought; no ancient image securely depicts a Druid.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: The account's rhetoric, sources, and relationship to archaeological evidence remain debated.
sacrificeEvidence.confidence: Allegation securely attested; practice not established by this source alone

sacrificeEvidence.title: Medieval blood-libel accusation
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: Blood libel falsely accused Jews of ritual murder. Atlas records the polemic and its consequences while marking the accusation false.
sacrificeEvidence.evidence: Historical documentation of a false accusation and persecution.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: The allegation is antisemitic propaganda, not evidence of Jewish ritual practice.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: No evidentiary ambiguity is suggested about the accusation's falsity.

sacrificeEvidence.title: Colonial-era descriptions of Mexica sacrifice
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: The Florentine Codex preserves Nahua testimony through a colonial Franciscan project. Its images and texts require attention to Indigenous collaborators, translation, colonial power, and genre.
sacrificeEvidence.evidence: Bilingual colonial manuscript testimony and images.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Created within a colonial missionary setting; neither discarded wholesale nor read transparently.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: Translation, editorial mediation, event scale, and representativeness need source-specific review.

sacrificeEvidence.title: Iphigenia sacrificial tradition
sacrificeEvidence.period: Ancient mythic and dramatic traditions with later reception
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: The sacrifice or substitution of Iphigenia appears in changing mythic and literary versions; it is not direct evidence for a specific historical killing.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Versions serve different dramatic, ritual, and interpretive purposes.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: Variant endings and relationships to historical ritual must remain visible.
sacrificeEvidence.confidence: Literary tradition secure; historical event not established

sacrificeEvidence.title: Modern reports of alleged ritual killings in Liberia
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: United Nations documents report allegations and calls for investigation. Atlas does not assert guilt, adjudication, or a generalized religious or ethnic practice.
sacrificeEvidence.evidence: International human-rights reporting of alleged cases and investigations.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: The sources use allegation language; reporting is not a criminal judgment.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: Case outcomes and evidentiary status require further reviewed sources.

sacrificeEvidence.title: Satanic ritual-abuse and sacrifice conspiracy claims
sacrificeEvidence.caseSummary: Claims of organized secret networks committing ritual sacrifice are recorded as a modern moral-panic and investigative-history topic, not as established criminal evidence.
sacrificeEvidence.evidence: Law-enforcement review of allegations and investigative indicators.
sacrificeEvidence.sourceBias: Reports must distinguish allegations, substantiated crimes, suggestive symbols, and repeated media narratives.
sacrificeEvidence.disagreement: Individual crimes require case evidence; broad hidden-network claims lack verified support in the cited review.
